broad_pool_narrow_safety_zone.headline: Your hero pool is wide. Your safety zone is not.
broad_pool_narrow_safety_zone.body: You explore broadly overall, but your history becomes more concentrated around familiar heroes when results are less stable.
broad_pool_narrow_safety_zone.interpretation: You do not avoid experimentation. You appear to rely on familiarity more selectively.
broad_pool_narrow_safety_zone.share: My hero pool is wide. Apparently my safety zone is not.

many_heroes_same_toolkit.headline: You play a lot of heroes. You keep rebuilding the same toolkit.
many_heroes_same_toolkit.body: {traits} keep showing up even as the hero changes.
many_heroes_same_toolkit.interpretation: Your pool is broader than a single hero, but the tools you reach for are more stable than the names on the screen.
many_heroes_same_toolkit.share: I play a lot of heroes. I keep rebuilding the same toolkit.

activity_travels_better_than_results.headline: Your activity survives new heroes better than your results do.
activity_travels_better_than_results.body: Your typical activity is {activity_read}; the larger change appears in the result signal, with familiar heroes ahead by {performance_gap}.
activity_travels_better_than_results.interpretation: You keep finding action outside your comfort pool. The gap appears later in converting that activity into results.
activity_travels_better_than_results.share: My activity travels farther than my results do.

losses_change_trust_more_than_pace.headline: Losses change what you trust more than how much you play.
losses_change_trust_more_than_pace.body: Familiar picks rise from {after_win} after wins to {after_loss} after losses, while the available pace signal stays comparatively close.
losses_change_trust_more_than_pace.interpretation: The visible change is selection, not a claim about mindset: after a loss, your history leans back toward known heroes.
losses_change_trust_more_than_pace.share: Losses change what I trust more than how much I play.

long_session_tax.headline: Your Dota changes after game three.
long_session_tax.body: Your later-session results are {delta} than games 1–3 in the same session, and your history regularly reaches game four or later.
long_session_tax.interpretation: The pattern is a queue condition worth testing, not a permanent label.
long_session_tax.share: My Dota changes after game three.

long_game_edge.headline: Your games age unusually well.
long_game_edge.body: Your long-game result signal is {delta} than the short-game signal in this history.
long_game_edge.interpretation: Long games are a context where more of your usual edge appears to survive.

long_game_leak.headline: The longer the game goes, the less your normal edge survives.
long_game_leak.body: Your long-game result signal is {delta} than the short-game signal in this history.
long_game_leak.interpretation: Duration is a context to simplify decisions around, not proof of a single underlying cause.
long_game_leak.share: The longer the game goes, the less my normal edge survives.

form_identity_divergence.headline: Your results changed faster than your playstyle.
form_identity_divergence.body: Recent form moved, while the style signal changed by only {style_delta}; the result shift is not the same thing as an identity shift.
form_identity_divergence.interpretation: Your current results may be moving through a familiar style rather than announcing a new player identity.
form_identity_divergence.share: My results changed faster than my playstyle.

strength_with_tax.headline: The thing that gives you {strength} also comes with a cost.
strength_with_tax.body: The same broad behavior that shows up as a strength is paired with {tax} in a different context.
strength_with_tax.interpretation: This is a compatibility pattern, not a causal verdict. Test the trade-off in a small window.
strength_with_tax.share: My strongest habit comes with a tax.

signature_hero_mechanism.headline: {hero} is not just your most-played comfort pick.
signature_hero_mechanism.body: It concentrates {traits}, the same tools your comfort pool keeps asking for.
signature_hero_mechanism.interpretation: Your signature hero is useful here as an explanation of the toolkit, not as a permanent identity label.
signature_hero_mechanism.share: My signature hero concentrates the toolkit I keep asking for.

role_vs_hero_identity.headline: You change heroes more than you change jobs.
role_vs_hero_identity.body: Your role signal is more stable than the names in your hero pool, so the role is carrying more identity than any one pick.
role_vs_hero_identity.interpretation: Your hero variety does not necessarily mean role variety. The job may be the through-line.
role_vs_hero_identity.share: I change heroes more than I change jobs.

volatile_results_stable_style.headline: Your bad games look worse than your actual playstyle changes.
volatile_results_stable_style.body: Results are volatile, while the available style signals stay within a relatively narrow band.
volatile_results_stable_style.interpretation: The history supports a stable style with uneven outcomes, without proving why individual games turn.
volatile_results_stable_style.share: My results swing harder than my playstyle does.

hidden_strength_fallback.headline: One of your strongest habits holds up across the history.
hidden_strength_fallback.interpretation: This is the clearest positive pattern available in the bounded summary history.
hidden_strength_fallback.share: One of my strongest Dota habits holds up across the history.
